records.title: Retention policy for replay-grade market snapshot history

body.rationale: EXP-0001 shows only ~45 days of full-fidelity instrument snapshots and ~51 days of heatmap history exist, far short of a 6-month replay goal. Compaction (hourly gzip archival) preserves history today, but prune_generated_state.py defaults would delete 627 artifacts (~1.1GB) if applied. Recommend: (1) disable or raise prune thresholds to 180 days or -1 for both instrument-snapshot-archives and relative-value-history; (2) keep compact_instrument_snapshots.py as-is (archive-only, never delete); (3) build replay harness to read archives not just hot JSONL; (4) do not run prune --apply until operator approves. Estimated retention cost: ~1.0-1.3 GB/month combined (snapshots ~1.0 GB/mo at ~1.6 MB/hour gz + RVH ~150 MB/mo). With 9.2 GB free, 180-day retention (~6 GB) is feasible without disk upgrade; 365-day would need monitoring or larger volume.

instrumentSnapshotArchives.action: raise prune --snapshot-archive-days to 180 or -1; never delete via manual prune without review

hotInstrumentSnapshots.action: no change; compaction already archives to gz

dailyValuationsMacro.action: keep append-only; fix merge-conflict tip rows separately

fundingHistory.action: derive from instrument snapshots; consider optional standalone funding JSONL export for lighter replays

pruneAutomation.action: do not schedule prune_generated_state.py --apply until policy approved

approvedPolicy.note: Operator approved 180-day VPS filesystem retention for replay-grade instrument-snapshot archives and relative-value history. Not Neon/Postgres. prune_generated_state.py and generated_state_health.py defaults raised 14/21 -> 180/180. No automated prune --apply scheduled.
approvedPolicy.clarification: This policy is for on-disk VPS artifacts (data/instrument-snapshot-archives, /var/lib/polymarket-trader/relative-value-history). Neon Postgres backups remain on polymarket-neon-backup.timer (separate).
approvedPolicy.operatorNote: Operator confirmed: full instrument snapshots and relative-value history stay on VPS disk (180-day retention). Neon remains for structured trade/ledger data and DB backups only — not full snapshot JSONL.

records.title: EXP: ex-ante confidence calibration audit (live trades, shadows, hypotheses)

body.question: Is the trading system's ex-ante confidence/probability well-calibrated against realized win rates, and which trade/shadow populations have a recoverable ex-ante confidence to test this at all?
body.method: scripts/confidence_calibration.py (stdlib-only) audits every candidate confidence source named in the Phase 3 brief by reading scripts/trading-engine.ts's Position/ClosedTrade interfaces and every named data file. It joins three verified-joinable sources to realized outcomes, buckets observations into fixed 0.2-wide confidence buckets, and computes gap = realizedWinRate - meanConfidence per (source, bucket). Excludes trades with close_reason=data_quality_artifact or id in operationally-tainted-trades.json, and shadows with hypotheticalResult.closeReason=data_quality_artifact or an unresolved outcome.

joinable: data/blocked-signals.json: 818 resolved shadow trades carry an ex-ante `confidence` (recorded at blockedAt) joined to hypotheticalResult.outcome (win/loss); 32 excluded as data_quality_artifact/unresolved. Spans 9 blockedReason families.
data/hypotheses.json: 581 triggered test events joined to each hypothesis's static ex-ante `confidence` (531 hypotheses, all with numeric confidence).
52 of 482 closed live trades (10.8%) join via a non-empty hypothesis_id to hypotheses.json confidence, after excluding 28 tainted/data_quality_artifact trades.
notJoinable: 402 of 482 closed live trades (89.2%) have NO recoverable ex-ante confidence: verified by reading the Position and ClosedTrade TypeScript interfaces in scripts/trading-engine.ts — neither persists a confidence/probability field — and trades-detailed.csv has no confidence column. Confidence is computed transiently in signal-generation code (e.g. `confidence: strength * weight.weight`) but discarded once a position opens.

data/candidate-actions.json entryCandidates[].confidence is real ex-ante confidence but the file is overwritten every engine run (current snapshot only, no history) — past candidates can't be joined back to the trades opened from them.
data/engine-state.json openPositions and data/position-snapshots.csv are derived point-in-time summaries with no confidence field.
data/calibration-buckets-summary.json stores only realized winRate for NO_BIAS_ADJUSTED_GAP_SHADOW shadows with no confidence field — outcome-only, not a calibration input.
data/llm-close-rejections.json, data/llm-state.json, data/llm-advice.json are operational logs of close decisions/skips; none store an entry-time win probability.

keyFindings: Systemic overconfidence at high confidence in hypothesis-derived populations: hypotheses_test_level bucket 0.6-0.8 (n=479) predicts 0.686 but realizes 0.399 (gap -0.287), and bucket 0.8-1.0 (n=99) predicts 0.818 but realizes 0.444 (gap -0.373). The same pattern repeats in the live-trade subset traceable to a hypothesis (live_trades_via_hypothesis 0.8-1.0, n=46, predicts 0.823, realizes 0.435, gap -0.388) — 'high confidence' hypotheses win less than half the time in both the paper test-event population and the live trades linked to them.

shadow:weekend_hl_funding_shadow is the single largest bucket in the dataset (n=254, confidence clustered at ~0.50) and realizes a 74.4% win rate — gap +0.244, substantially underconfident. This is the strategy backing STRAT-0001 (currently active live).

shadow:short_blocked_by_positive_trend at confidence 0.0-0.2 (n=23) realizes a 56.5% win rate versus a predicted 7.4% (gap +0.491): signals the engine blocks specifically for having low computed confidence actually win more than half the time in this sample.

records.title: Persist ex-ante confidence per trade on live positions/ledger

body.rationale: EXP-0003 found that 89.2% of closed live trades have zero recoverable ex-ante confidence: scripts/trading-engine.ts's Position and ClosedTrade interfaces never persist the confidence value that IS computed at signal-generation time (e.g. `confidence: strength * weight.weight`), and trades-detailed.csv has no confidence column. The only live-trade confidence signal available today is an indirect, coarse proxy: joining via hypothesis_id to a hypothesis's single static confidence value (10.8% coverage). Meanwhile the shadow-trade population (blocked-signals.json) shows this is a solvable problem — it already persists confidence per shadow instance at blockedAt and enables real calibration analysis today. Persisting the same per-instance ex-ante confidence on live Position/ClosedTrade records (not just the hypothesis's static value) would let calibration audits, Kelly-sizing work, and signal-weight tuning use the full live population instead of an ~11% joinable slice.
body.proposedChange: Add a `confidence: number` field to the Position and ClosedTrade interfaces in scripts/trading-engine.ts, populated from the signal's `confidence` at the moment a position is opened (the same value already computed and used for sizing/ranking), and add a matching `confidence` column to trades-detailed.csv's writer/reader so it survives to the ledger. No change to sizing, entry logic, stops, or targets.

implemented.note: New opens persist ex-ante confidence; pre-existing ledger rows remain blank.

records.title: DEC: replay clock injection via preload (REPLAY_NOW_MS), no engine patch

body.rationale: The trading engine has dozens of new Date()/Date.now() call sites, including the America/New_York weekend-window gate isStockPerpFundingWindowOpen(). To replay a past hour deterministically the clock must be injected everywhere. The replay harness freezes the global Date in a NODE --import preload (scripts/replay-preload.mjs) to REPLAY_NOW_MS, rather than patching engine source.
body.decision: Use approach (c): a tsx/node preload that fakes Date globally for the child process, plus an offline fetch stub. NO engine source was patched for the replay.
body.inertness: replay-preload.mjs early-returns when REPLAY_NOW_MS is unset/invalid, so it is a strict no-op for any normal production run and only affects processes the harness explicitly launches with REPLAY_NOW_MS set. There is therefore no change to production engine behavior and nothing to review/commit in trading-engine.ts.
alternativesConsidered: (a) reuse an existing engine env var for the clock: rejected - none exists; resolveEnginePathConfig/parseEngineCliFlags expose no clock override.

(b) minimal engine patch adding REPLAY_NOW_MS support at each new Date()/Date.now(): rejected - touches the hot production decision path in many places, needs careful review, and carries behavior-risk for a live paper trader; the preload achieves the same determinism with zero engine edits.
body.networkNeutralization: The same preload replaces globalThis.fetch with an empty-JSON (HTTP 200 []) stub so Polymarket Gamma/CLOB book lookups degrade to null gracefully (fetchMarketYesNoBooks returns null; openPositions does not throw). Combined with --no-llm (callLLM never invoked) this guarantees zero network egress and zero LLM token spend during replay.
body.isolation: DATA_DIR = join(import.meta.dirname,'..','data') is not env-redirectable, so the harness copies the scripts/ tree into the sandbox; the engine then resolves DATA_DIR and the default live-state dir inside the sandbox (POLYMARKET_TRADER_STATE_DIR is also set to <sandbox>/.runtime). No production state (data/, /var/lib/polymarket-trader) is ever written.

records.title: EXP: deterministic replay harness validation vs production weekend HL funding (2026-07-10..14)

body.question: Does a deterministic offline replay of scripts/trading-engine.ts over archived hourly instrument snapshots reproduce production's weekend Hyperliquid stock-perp funding-reversion (WEEKEND_HL_FUNDING_REVERSION_LONG) trades for 2026-07-10..2026-07-14 (the last weekend gate)?
body.method: Isolated sandbox replay (scripts/replay-harness.ts). DATA_DIR is not env-redirectable (join(import.meta.dirname,'..','data')), so the whole scripts/ tree is copied into /tmp/replay-1/scripts and the engine reads/writes only /tmp/replay-1/data. Per replay hour T the harness reconstructs inputs: 12-snapshot lookback (option-stripped, mirroring readInstrumentSnapshotPrefix) from data/instrument-snapshot-archives/*.gz + hot file, daily-valuations/daily-macro truncated to date<=T, closest relative-value-history CSV <=T, a fresh $100 portfolio, empty ledger and empty blocked-signals. Determinism: global Date frozen to T via a NODE --import preload (REPLAY_NOW_MS); fetch replaced with an empty-JSON offline stub; engine run with --no-llm (zero token spend). 116 hourly engine invocations. Comparison (scripts/replay_compare.py) matches on asset+entry-hour vs production data/trades-detailed.csv.
body.conclusion: PASS. The replay reproduces every one of the 37 production weekend-funding entries (0 missed) on the same asset+entry-hour, with matched-trade P&L near-identical (max abs diff 0.0011, correlation 1.0) and matching close reasons. The mechanical exits (target/24h-expiry/funding-normalize/window-close) fire per the rules. The only divergence is 39 extra re-entries (mostly Jul 12-13) fully explained by the fresh-portfolio, empty-blocked-signals design (no re-entry dedup / slot occupancy / shadow suppression that constrained production).
limitations: Fresh empty portfolio + empty blocked-signals: no position/shadow carry-over from before the window, so production's re-entry dedup (skip if a weekend-funding position or shadow is already open for an asset) and 15-slot/$100 occupancy are not reproduced -> 39 extra re-entries on Jul 12-13 after Jul 11 positions close.

Static configs (learning-params.json, signal-weights.json, hypotheses.json) copied as an as-of-now snapshot; intra-window config drift is not reconstructed. Weekend-funding entry/exit logic is hardcoded (ENABLE=true, band [-100%,-50%], 10% funding exit, 3% target, 24h, 5x) and independent of these configs, so it is unaffected.
Snapshots are hour-granular and option-stripped (exactly what the engine reads); ~13% of calendar hours have no archived snapshot and are skipped.

Polymarket Gamma/CLOB fetches are neutralized offline, so any polymarket entry path is inert; the replay is faithful only for snapshot-driven signals (weekend HL funding and other Hyperliquid/valuation-driven signals).
LLM disabled (--no-llm), so any LLM-gated closes/entries that occurred in production are absent by design.

records.title: Phase A: permanent FIND records with provenance

body.rationale: Phase A stats-first research loop stores mined shadow clusters as FIND records (clusterKey upsert) with immutable provenance and evidence {n, winRate, sumPnl}. Auto H-* hypothesis promotion from shadow mine is deferred to Phase D; nightly runs mine_shadow_findings.py instead of mine_shadow_hypotheses.py.

records.title: Phase B: dual opportunity/confidence scoring for FIND records

body.rationale: Phase B adds deterministic dual scores on every FIND: opportunityScore (should we investigate?) and confidenceScore (how much evidence?). score_research_findings.py (research_score_v1) writes scoreHistory and ranked data/research-opportunities.json for Phase D nightly LLM consumption.

Weekend Hyperliquid funding reversion shadows
Phase C: research themes grouping FIND records

body.rationale: Phase C groups FIND records into coarse Research Themes (THEME-*) via deterministic signal-family slugs. assign_research_themes.py sets finding.body.themeId and theme.links.findings, and writes data/research-themes.json for Phase D hypothesis authorship.

records.title: Phase D: nightly LLM authors hypotheses from ranked FIND opportunities

body.rationale: Phase D closes the stats-invent/LLM-experiment loop: deterministic mining and scoring select top-N FIND opportunities, while the nightly LLM may author new hypotheses only from those ranked findings. Each LLM hypothesis must carry originFindingId and themeId when available so engine ingest can preserve provenance and update FIND registry links.

records.title: Phase E: nightly research report for operators

body.rationale: Phase E aggregates ranked FIND opportunities, research themes, and nightly LLM-authored hypotheses into data/nightly-research-report.md and .json. build_nightly_research_report.py runs after shadow mining and nightly-research.ts; the morning daily Telegram report surfaces a truncated Nightly Research Loop section so operators see evidence-first context instead of journal-only writeups.

records.title: Phase F: negative FIND writeback from failed hypotheses

body.rationale: Phase F closes the FIND→hypothesis→experiment loop: when a hypothesis with originFindingId fails (killed/archived or >=5 resolved tests with winRate < 0.40), writeback_negative_findings.py marks the FIND status=negative and links the failed hyp id. upsert_finding never reopens negative records on re-mine; score_research_findings excludes negatives from opportunities.

records.title: Phase G: attach replay evidence to top FIND opportunities

body.rationale: Replay evidence should be attached only to the highest-opportunity FIND records, not every mined finding. Nightly writes a cheap reproducible replay plan by default and performs short real attachments only when FIND_REPLAY_ATTACH=1 is set, preserving the research loop without adding routine VPS load.

records.title: Hypothesis shadow backfill fill-rate policy

body.rationale: Historical backfill should measure whether hypotheses would have triggered on available history without letting metadata-only fields or future-dated pendings suppress eligible tests. The policy keeps real metric misses visible, uses archived relative-value observations where available, and separates live retest fan-out from historical backfill accounting.
body.decision: Use backfill-only metadata handling, archived relative-value snapshots, and historical pending resolution before target caps; keep raised live retest concurrency caps.
policy: Treat venue, asset, signalType, and day_of_week as metadata during historical backfill unless clearly false; evaluate day_of_week from the row date when possible.
Skip unknown non-numeric condition keys with warning counts, but keep metric-like missing keys as hard failures and report them.
Resolve historically mature pending tests before opening new backfill tests and do not let future-dated pendings occupy historical target slots.
Include LLM/FIND-linked and shadow_mined setup families in backfill eligibility under the 20-test target.
Use latest daily archived relative-value snapshots for historical FIND and settlement-bucket conditions.
Live LLM/FIND retests are capped at 200 active / 8 pending per family; shadow_mined retests at 80 active / 4 pending per family.
body.validation: Dry-run improved expanded eligible-under-20 families from 22 to 15, with AMZN/HYPE 19+pending families reaching 20 completed.

records.title: Informed flow asymmetry: dip-YES flow is smart money, high-YES flow is dumb money (wallet-level study)

body.summary: Wallet-level study of resolved touch markets: walk-forward wallet skill is persistent (Spearman ~0.22). Smart-wallet share of net-YES is higher on dips than highs; dumb-wallet share is higher on highs. Lead-lag: dip-YES richening precedes spot declines; high-YES richening does not precede rallies. Entry-time flow adds little AUC beyond PM price.
body.implication: Sell-YES / buy-NO edges vs the options model are trustworthy on highs (fading dumb lottery flow) and unreliable on dips (fighting informed fear flow). Gate one-touch and NO-bias entries by direction: keep highs, downweight or block dips; when smart_flow_stance is known, require stance <= 0 to fade.
